sections.h2: What does the Forsyth County Clerk of Superior Court record?
sections.html:
The clerk records and indexes real estate in Forsyth County: deeds, plats, condominium floor plans, UCC filings, General Execution Docket entries, lien filings and military discharges. A sale of any Forsyth County house, in Cumming or elsewhere, sends the buyer's deed to this office, along with the cancellation of your security deed once the loan is paid off.

The Real Estate division answers at 770-781-2120 (choose option 6) or at RealEstate@forsythco.com. The clerk's letterhead gives the courthouse address as 101 E. Courthouse Square, Cumming, GA 30040. The clerk's site also offers a property index search, a forms page, a link to a property and mortgage fraud check, and a map viewer for abstractors.

sections.h2: What are the Forsyth County clerk's recording fees?
sections.html:
A deed, quit claim deed or similar real estate document costs $25.00 to record, and extra pages are included. Security deed cancellations, releases and assignments are also $25.00 each. The table below repeats the lines most sellers meet at closing, taken from the clerk's posted schedule.

Selected Forsyth County clerk fees (Forsyth County Clerk of Superior Court, Court Costs and Recording Fees)
ItemFee
Deed, quit claim, modification, assignment of leases and rents (each)$25.00, added pages included
Security deed cancellation, release or assignment$25.00, added pages included
General Execution Docket or lien filing$25.00
UCC filing$25.00
Certified copy$2.50 first page, $0.50 each added page
Regular copy$0.50 per page
Copy needing staff help$1.00 per page
Oversize copy (bigger than 8.5 by 14 inches)$2.00 per page

Call the Real Estate division for a total before mailing a check; this schedule shows the clerk's charge alone. Transfer tax and any intangible recording tax are billed separately.

sections.h2: Who pays transfer tax on a Forsyth County deed?
sections.html:
Payment comes first: the clerk stamps a paid certification onto the deed, then records it. The state rate works out to $1 on the opening $1,000 of price and ten cents per additional $100 or part.

Sellers owe it unless the contract says the buyer pays, and the settlement statement shows which happened. The PT-61 declaration is filed online through the state clerks' authority, and the Forsyth clerk's menu links to it. A question about exemptions goes to this clerk, as the Department of Revenue directs.

sections.h2: What is the intangible recording tax on a mortgage?
sections.html:
This is a separate state charge on lenders and borrowers, and a seller handing over a deed does not owe it. The security instrument behind a new loan has to be recorded within 90 days, and the rate the state prints is $1.50 per $500 of note, with a partial $500 counted in full.

Most counties route it through the clerk. Your settlement statement shows whether any of it applies to your closing.

sections.h2: How does e-filing a deed work in Forsyth County?
sections.html:
The clerk's site sends real estate e-filers to efile.gsccca.org. Since January 1, 2025, anyone who files real estate documents electronically there must upload government-issued photo identification, such as a driver's license or passport, and have it verified before the filing can go forward.

If you plan to bring a deed yourself, call the Real Estate division and ask which filing methods it accepts for your situation, plus how your payment should be made out. The clerk's FAQ page lists questions about checks, card payments, witnesses and notarizing, so check it before you drive to the courthouse.

sections.h2: How do liens, tax executions and unpaid property tax connect to the clerk?
sections.html:
When county tax goes unpaid the Tax Commissioner can issue a Fi.Fa., a lien that lands on the clerk's General Execution Docket. It lasts seven years unless paid off, and the payoff covers the tax plus fees, penalties and interest. A warning letter with a 30-day window comes first.

  • A lien on the docket is a public record, so expect it to be raised when the buyer's side searches title.
  • The cancellation is itself a filing at the clerk's counter, with the lien fee shown in the table above.
  • Any tax sale is an auction on the courthouse steps in Cumming, held on a first Tuesday.

The tax commissioner's property tax page also asks sellers to email the closing statement to the tax office so the next bill goes to the new owner's name, provided the purchase closed before November 15.

The PT-61 filed with the clerk does a second job for the buyer. When the property was not subdivided, changed or improved and the transfer tax was paid, the tax commissioner says that form can stand in as the new owner's property tax return, and the preceding year's final valuation is treated as the returned value unless a new return is filed with the Board of Assessors.

sections.h2: How do I get a copy of a recorded Forsyth County document?
sections.html:
The Copy Requests page quotes statutory prices under O.C.G.A. 15-6-77: half a dollar a page for a standard copy, a dollar a page for non-standard, and $2.50 for the first page of a certified copy with 50 cents per page after that. Non-standard means unscanned, odd-sized or atypical records that need hands-on help from staff.

You can also search the property index on the clerk's website to see whether a cancellation of your old security deed was filed. If it is missing, call your loan servicer first and then the Real Estate division.

sections.h2: What else does the Forsyth County clerk file that touches a home sale?
sections.html:
The same posted fee sheet that prices deeds lists a few other items owners run into. A veteran who needs a military discharge copy pays nothing but must show valid identification. Notary authentication costs $3.00, and a new or renewed notary commission is $55.00. Registering a trade name for a rental or flipping business costs $175.00 as a filing fee, which excludes newspaper publication.

Lawsuits are a separate track. The clerk's civil division in Superior and State Court takes e-filings through two vendors, PeachCourt and a Tyler Technologies portal, and the E-File page links to both. A lawsuit over a sale contract would start there instead of at the Real Estate counter.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Forsyth County sellers?
sections.html:
Census Bureau QuickFacts counts 282,805 residents in Forsyth County as of July 2025, a 12.5 percent gain since April 2020, on roughly 224.62 square miles of land. The housing stock totals 98,879 units, and owners live in 84.4 percent of occupied homes. Homes that owners occupy have a median value of $550,400 (2020 to 2024 survey), while the typical household earns $143,784.

With values that high, a clean deed and a paid-up tax account matter a great deal to a buyer's lender. The clerk's office is in the courthouse at the county seat, Cumming.

  • Median gross rent in the same survey was $2,090.
  • The county issued 1,743 building permits in 2025.
  • Foreign-born residents make up 22.9 percent of the population, and 27.7 percent speak another language at home.

faqs.q: Where does a Forsyth County deed get recorded?
faqs.a: The clerk's Real Estate division, in Cumming. Phone 770-781-2120 and choose option 6, or write to RealEstate@forsythco.com.

faqs.q: What is the Forsyth County recording charge for a deed?
faqs.a: $25.00 for a deed, quit claim or similar document, and added pages cost nothing extra. Transfer tax is a separate charge.

faqs.q: Who owes the Georgia transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The seller, unless the sales contract moves it to the buyer. The state requires payment before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Do I need ID to e-file a real estate document in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. Since January 1, 2025, anyone e-filing real estate documents through the Georgia clerks' portal must upload government-issued ID and pass verification first.

faqs.q: Can an unpaid tax bill stop my Forsyth County sale?
faqs.a: It can slow one down. A recorded Fi.Fa. on the clerk's docket is public and stays until the tax, fees, penalties and interest are paid, so get a payoff figure from the Forsyth County Tax Commissioner before closing.
